messages.subject: Introductory NIMBLE Workshop, Switzerland, April 2018
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

from 23-25 April 2018 Michael Schaub and I are hosting a Nimble introductory workshop taught by Perry de Valpine (University of California, Berkeley), see attachment and also here: http://www.phidot.org/forum/viewtopic.php?f=8&t=3586

Nimble is the latest member of the software family for fitting hierarchical models that uses the BUGS language to describe the model. In our opinion this is almost a prerequisite for wide adoption by ecologist and other non-statisticians. Nimble offers exciting capabilities to extend the functionality, customize the MCMC samplers and allows fitting of hierarchical models by likelihood methods.

Best regards  --- Marc Kéry

messages.subject: Re: Introductory NIMBLE Workshop, Switzerland, April 2018
messages.body_plain:
In a nutshell: NIMBLE makes both the BUGS model language and algorithms that use models extensible.  You can add new functions and distributions.  You can customize choice of samplers, write new samplers, and write/use other methods (not just MCMC).  Models and algorithms are compiled by generating and compiling C++, so everything can run fast.  We do have relatively new support for CAR models, and there is room for anyone to contribute improved general or case-specific methods.  If you write something that you want to share, you can contribute to NIMBLE or write your own R package that uses NIMBLE.  Something like BART regression trees would be an interesting case for adding new functions, distributions and samplers to support these models.  If there are external libraries you want to use, you can have the compiled NIMBLE code call externally compiled code.  For more information (including a full user manual), please see http:r-nimble.org <http://r-nimble.org>

While I have the floor: we are hiring a post-doc!  Please see https://r-nimble.org/nimble-has-a-post-doc-or-software-developer-position-open

Perry

messages.subject: Post doc @ MSU - monarch butterfly modeling project
messages.subject_clean: Post doc @ MSU - monarch butterfly modeling project
messages.body_plain:
Please distribute widely! Start date is flexible.

Thanks,

Elise

___________________________________

The Zipkin Quantitative Ecology Lab seeks a postdoctoral scholar to work with a team of researchers on an NSF funded project to develop integrated, hierarchical statistical models to estimate and predict monarch butterfly demography across eastern North America. Project goals include tracking dynamics at each life history stage of this unique and iconic migratory species to 1) determine which stage(s) and environmental variables may be driving observed declines, and 2) predict impacts of climate and resource change on future population abundance. Data come from several continental-scale, volunteer-based monitoring programs. Our team (led by Elise Zipkin and Leslie Ries) has gathered and formatted the monitoring data and a processing platform has been built to extract relevant climate and environmental variables from appropriate databases. The postdoctoral scholar will work collaboratively to develop models, carry out analyses, and write manuscripts. The richness of the datasets allows for ample ability to explore many avenues of research and we seek a researcher with enthusiasm to pursue related projects that interests them.

Qualifications: Applicants must hold a PhD in ecology, biology, statistics, or a related field by the start of the position. Applicants are expected to have a strong background in mathematical and/or statistical modeling, ecology, and experience publishing scientific research. Knowledge of program R is required. Candidates with experience in Bayesian hierarchical analysis, integrated models, the BUGS language, and collaborative research are especially encouraged to apply.

The position is based at Michigan State University (MSU) with opportunities to travel to meet with collaborators, attend workshops and conferences, and become involved in other lab projects. The position comes with a competitive salary and excellent health benefits. This is a full-time, 12-month, fixed-term position, with reappointment conditional on satisfactory performance. To apply, email as a single PDF: 1) a cover letter (2-pg max) with your research interests and qualifications for this position, 2) CV, 3) list of three references with contact information, and 4) one recent first-authored publication, to Dr. Elise Zipkin, Department of Integrative Biology, MSU (ezi...@msu.edu). Please use the subject heading “PostDoc Application”.

The position will remain open until filled.
